_doc: Bambu Lab X1 Carbon with the stock 0.4 mm nozzle and Bambu Studio defaults. kind: spec (manufacturer), default (slicer setting), community (widely used rule of thumb), measured (your own test print; beats the rest), estimate (a reasoned guess: measure it).
name: x1c

line.rule: Bambu Studio's default line width for a 0.4 mm nozzle: walls are whole numbers of lines
line.source: Bambu Studio 0.4 mm nozzle process profile

layer.rule: Default layer height; heights that matter should be whole numbers of layers

wall_min.rule: Thinnest wall worth printing: two lines

hole_comp.rule: Printed holes and slots come out small: widen them by this much
hole_comp.source: Common FDM practice; tune with a test print

fit.rule: Gap between parts that slide together
fit.source: Common FDM practice; tune with a test print

press.rule: How much smaller across a printed bore is than a bought part pressed into it, once printed (a ball bearing's outer race): hole_comp is added as well
press.source: A reasoned guess, half a typical 0.1 mm hole error; measure it with the seats coupon (examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/objects/seats-coupon)

slip.rule: How much larger across a printed bore is than a bought part that slides into it by hand, once printed: hole_comp is added as well
slip.source: A reasoned guess; measure it with the seats coupon (examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/objects/seats-coupon)

print_flow.rule: Average plastic laid per second over a whole print, walls, travel and all: for estimating minutes from a part's volume
print_flow.source: A rule of thumb for a 0.4 mm nozzle on default settings; check it against a real print's time

print_gap.rule: Narrowest gap between parts printed in place, side by side, that still prints apart (a flexure and the frame round it, a shuttle in its slot): the gap each side, not the total
print_gap.source: A reasoned guess for a 0.42 mm line; measure it with the fit test plate (examples/bench/projects/launcher/objects/fittest)

overhang.rule: Steepest overhang from vertical that prints without supports

bridge.rule: Widest gap a flat underside can span with no support (the widest circle that fits in it)

support_gap.rule: Gap between a built-in breakaway support and the part: one layer, so it snaps off

chamfer.rule: Chamfer bottom edges instead of rounding them, against first-layer squish

foot.rule: How far the first layer spreads each side as it is squashed on to the bed (elephant's foot): two parts printed in place must stand print_gap plus twice this apart there, or they print as one
foot.source: Bambu Studio's default elephant foot compensation, 0.15 mm, the amount it shrinks the first layer by to undo the spread

thread_gap.rule: Gap between the flanks of a printed screw thread and the thread it screws into, measured on the radius (twice this across the diameter). A printed pair is drawn half of it each; a printed thread for a bought screw or nut takes all of it. An internal thread gets hole_comp as well, as any printed hole does
thread_gap.source: A reasoned guess, the same as fit, the gap between parts that slide together; the fixings coupon prints M6 to M12 threads at three clearances to measure it (docs/fixings-and-frames.md, section 2.5)

snap_clearance.rule: Gap round a printed snap pin's peg in its socket, each side, as drawn: the socket's hole is the peg's diameter plus twice this, with no hole compensation added. Tighter, and the split halves cannot close to let the barb through; looser, and the pin rocks
snap_clearance.source: The clearance @rulecad/flexures' snapSocket drew by default before snap pins moved to @rulecad/fixings, kept so no socket moves; the holds coupon's snap pin socket rows, S3 and S4, measure it (examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/MEASURE.md row 41)

pin_press.rule: How much smaller across a printed hole is drawn than a plain pin pressed into it (a steel dowel, a length of filament): the pin grips. hole_comp is added as well, as for any printed hole
pin_press.source: A reasoned guess, the same as press, the bought bearing's press fit; the holds coupon's pressed pin rows, D3P and FP, print three press fits round it to measure it (examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/MEASURE.md row 42)

pin_slip.rule: How much larger across a printed hole is drawn than a plain pin that turns in it (a hinge pin): it slides in by hand and turns freely. hole_comp is added as well, as for any printed hole
pin_slip.source: A reasoned guess, the same as fit, the gap between parts that slide together; the holds coupon's slipping pin rows, D3S and FS, print three slip fits round it to measure it (examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/MEASURE.md row 43)

magnet_press.rule: How much smaller across a printed pocket is drawn than a disc or block magnet pressed into it, so it grips with no glue. hole_comp is added as well, as for any printed hole. A magnet is sold within ±0.1 mm (magnets.tolerance), so a press is a close call: crush ribs (magnet_crush) take up the spread
magnet_press.source: A reasoned guess, twice x1c.press since a magnet is sold to ±0.1 mm where a bearing is ground to microns; the holds coupon's magnet rows, 6x3 and 8x3, print three press fits round it to measure it (examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/MEASURE.md row 44)

magnet_glue.rule: How much larger across a printed pocket is drawn than a magnet glued into it: room for a film of glue, a twentieth of a millimetre each side. hole_comp is added as well
magnet_glue.source: A reasoned guess: the magnet catch of @rulecad/frames has drawn its pocket the magnet and x1c.fit (0.2 mm) across since 0.1, which is hole_comp and this. No coupon prints a glued pocket: examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/MEASURE.md row 44 says to keep it unless a glued magnet will not go in, and then to raise it by 0.1

magnet_crush.rule: With crush ribs, how much smaller across the ribs' tips stand than the magnet, past hole_comp: the ribs are a line wide and give, so a magnet anywhere in its ±0.1 mm goes in and grips
magnet_crush.source: A reasoned guess, twice magnets.tolerance; the holds coupon's crush rib row, 8x3R, measures it (examples/bench/projects/benchmarks/MEASURE.md row 45)

pilot_m3.rule: Hole to draw for an M3 screw to form its own thread in PLA: 2.9 mm and 3.0 mm drawn both hold the screw straight, and smaller holes send it in at an angle. Drawn as it is: no hole compensation
